title: After 2 nm: will graphene replace silicon? (article and citable PDF)
gist: Dr. Amir Al Herani summarises his article on post-2nm logic: '2 nm' is a label (gate pitch ~45 nm, gate length ~12 nm), scaling limits come from electrostatics and tunnelling, pristine graphene lacks a bandgap, MoS2 is the 2D material closest to a logic channel, and he puts <5% odds on graphene replacing silicon logic by 2040 vs >95% silicon remaining the main substrate.

insights.claim: The '2 nm' node name is a label: 2021 IRDS targets for this generation put contacted gate pitch near 45 nm, tightest metal pitch near 20 nm and physical gate length flattening around 12 nm.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Node names are marketing; compare foundries on actual pitches and density.
insights.quote: The node name is a label.
insights.locator: 1. The node name is a label.

insights.claim: TSMC has not disclosed the physical dimensions of its N2 transistor, but neither its gate length nor its pitch is 2 nm.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Don't infer physical scaling from node naming in TSMC comparisons.
insights.locator: 1. The node name is a label.

insights.claim: Transistor scaling limits arrive through electrostatics and tunnelling, quantified via WKB transmission through the source-drain barrier, the natural length lambda and subthreshold swing.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Physics, not lithography alone, caps silicon gate-length scaling, driving GAA/CFET and new channel materials.

insights.claim: Pristine graphene has no bandgap, which is why large-area graphene FETs commonly showed room-temperature on/off ratios below about ten.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Graphene is unsuitable as a digital switch without bandgap engineering; discount 'graphene replaces silicon' hype.

insights.claim: The 2024 semiconducting epigraphene result, with a bandgap near 0.6 eV grown on SiC, is important but far from 300 mm integration.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Epigraphene is a research milestone, not a near-term manufacturing story.

insights.claim: Graphene's more plausible roles are outside the digital channel, in specialised wiring and optical components of chips that remain predominantly silicon.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Graphene opportunities lie in interconnect and photonics niches, not logic transistors.

insights.claim: MoS2 is the 2D material closest to a logic channel, demonstrated in a 2025 32-bit RISC-V processor with about 5,900 transistors.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Track MoS2 as the leading 2D channel candidate for post-silicon-scaling logic.

insights.claim: imec, ASML and TSMC reported complementary MoS2 devices on a 300 mm wafer at a 50 nm contacted poly pitch in June 2026.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Major-ecosystem 300 mm 2D work signals TSMC/ASML are de-risking post-silicon channel options.

insights.claim: The author estimates below 5% probability that pristine graphene replaces silicon as the mainstream digital logic channel by 2040.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Strongly contrarian to graphene hype; low odds of disruption to silicon fab economics.
insights.quote: pristine graphene replacing silicon as the mainstream digital logic channel by 2040, below 5%

insights.claim: The author puts roughly even odds on a 2D semiconductor such as MoS2 entering at least some leading-edge logic-channel applications by 2040.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: 2D-material process/tooling suppliers are a plausible long-dated option.

insights.claim: The author estimates above 95% probability that silicon is still the main substrate for advanced logic manufacturing in 2040.
insights.speaker: U
insights.so_what: Silicon-centric fab and equipment investment remains durable through 2040.
